classification.difficultyReason: Derive a linear demand model, form a quadratic profit function and interpret its maximum with monetary rounding.

content.prompt: Frank has a coffee cart. It costs him $\$0.25$ to make each coffee. If he charges $\$4$ per cup, then he will sell 50 coffees. If he charges $\$3$ per coffee, then he will sell 80 coffees. Assume the number of coffees that he sells is a linear function of the price charged per coffee. What should he charge per coffee to maximise his profit? Give your answer correct to the nearest 5 cents.

answer.short:
$\$2.95$ per coffee.

Model the number sold by $N=170-30x$ and maximise $P=(x-0.25)(170-30x)$ using the midpoint of its intercepts.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the price per coffee in dollars and $N$ the number sold. Write $N=ax+b$.

$$\begin{align*}50&=4a+b\\80&=3a+b\\-30&=a\\b&=50-4(-30)\\b&=170\\N&=170-30x\end{align*}$$

Profit equals profit per coffee multiplied by the number sold:

$$\begin{align*}P&=(x-0.25)N\\P&=(x-0.25)(170-30x)\end{align*}$$

The profit parabola opens downwards and has intercepts $x=\frac14$ and $x=\frac{17}{3}$. Its maximum occurs halfway between them:

$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{\frac14+\frac{17}{3}}{2}\\x&=\frac{71}{24}\end{align*}$$

Rounded to the nearest 5 cents, Frank should charge $\$2.95$ per coffee.
